doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

chapter: Civil rights era and his mother's example
title: Empathy, giving, and the three types of people
summary: Griffin says his mother's lesson of giving shapes his art, and quotes a friend's givers, takers and users.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: That kind of empathy and character it seems has stayed with you. Do you believe it’s found its way into your composing and your visual artwork?

Oh sure, yeah. More and more now, like I say the older I get the more I really refer back to what my mother taught me and how it’s better to give and it’s kind of unpopular to be counting now, because people take advantage of that, you know take kindness as a weakness. They were — you know if you give them something people think they’re getting over on you, they’re thinking oh everybody — not everybody but a lot of people are hustling and trying to take as much as — there’s three types of people — this one of my friends named Johnny Grimes, he told me there’s three types of people in the world. There’s givers, there’s takers, and there’s users. The users and takers fall in the same group a lot. But the givers are just unique. And what you give is what you get. If you give love and compassion and understanding you get it. It might not come in the form that you want to but you get it you know. But if you give a lot of hustling and untruthful and getting over people, you’ll get it. It’ll come back at you. That’s the law of nature.
